A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same S2Q research work. All 33 pages of each version, including Appendices A–H, are available and readable; text, equations, tables and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original matrix-game simulations, MARL benchmark experiments, ablations, trajectory analyses and computational-cost measurements in Sections 4–5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results, including SMAC and GRF comparisons, supplementary experiments and runtime/memory measurements.

M1.justification: The successive sub-value learning objectives, Softmax selection, communication mechanism and S2Q-Comm variant are unchanged. Algorithms 1 and C.1 and the implementation procedures in Appendix C match.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same matrix game, SMAC-Hard+, GRF, SMAC-Comm, SMACv2 and SMAC-Hard (Mixture Opponent) scenarios. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main and appendix comparisons, including Figures 5–6, G.1–G.2 and H.3 and Table G.1. Updated citations for methods such as NDQ, VDN and QPLEX identify the same methods.

E3.justification: Evaluation procedures, metrics, training budgets and configurations remain unchanged. Tables F.1–F.2 retain the same settings, including batch size 128 and S2Q parameters K=2 and T=0.1.

E4.justification: The component ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity studies, exploration and trajectory analyses, auxiliary-supervision controls and computational-cost comparisons in Sections 5.2–5.3 and Appendices D and H are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Section 5 retains the same statement about reporting means and standard deviations across five random seeds. Uncertainty displays are unchanged, and no statistical estimation or testing procedure is added.

E6.justification: Result entries, plotted curves and reported findings match throughout both PDFs. For example, Table 1 retains S2Q at 73.43±5.29 and QMIX at 43.94±10.06; Tables G.1 and H.1–H.2 also retain their values.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.1, its restatement and proof in Appendix B, bounded-reward and suppression assumptions, and mathematical definitions and derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: tracking alternative high-value actions, adapting to shifting optima, improving exploration and outperforming MARL baselines. Their scientific scope and strength are unchanged.

C2.justification: Explanations of coordinated exploration, shifting action preferences and performance gains are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same computation/memory and temperature-selection limitations, with the same appendix discussion.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the direct repository address github.com/hyeon1996/S2Q with the project-site address hyeon1996.github.io/s2q/. Implementation, hardware and hyperparameter disclosures are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish any change to the code itself or its availability.

R1.justification: Section 3.1 adds Lee et al. (2026) on skill learning and Park et al. (2025) on a focusing influence mechanism. The introduction and bibliography remove Shalev-Shwartz et al. (2016) on autonomous driving. These are limited citation changes without substantive revision of the research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 adds the ICLR 2026 publication header and updates citation years, labels and bibliographic publication details for several existing works. The main exposition, section ordering and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The publication header and revised references produce limited layout and line-wrapping changes. Figures and tables retain their graphics, placement, structure, captions, axes and legends.

improvement.justification: V2 chiefly refreshes publication labeling, references and the code-access address. The limited citation changes leave the scientific exposition, evidence, theory and limitations unchanged, while the PDFs do not establish improved resource availability. These edits provide no meaningful overall quality difference.
